newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian Synod urges opening secret police files.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian Synod urges opening secret police files.

text.p: Bulgaria's Orthodox Church Holy Synod on Friday asked President Petar Stoyanov to order the opening of secret police files kept by the former communist government on its clergymen.
The church is split between followers of Patriarch Maxim and rebels who say he lacks authority because he was appointed, not elected, to his post in 1971 by the former communist authorities.

"We appeal to President Petar Stoyanov to order within 10 days the opening of the secret police files of all prelates, clergymen and officials of the Bulgarian Orthodox Church," a statement from Maxim's synod, carried by the state news agency BTA, said.
The statement said opening the secret police files ahead of the country's general election on April 19 would help Bulgarians to separate religious and moral issues from political concerns.

Rebel priests last summer enthrowned metropolitan Pimen as patriarch in defiance of church authorities. Pimen, who is close to the anti-communist Union of Democratic Forces (UDF), conducted the blessing ceremony when Stoyanov took office in January.

Earlier this month the Supreme Administrative Court declared the registration of Maxim's synod invalid for technical reasons. Maxim, who has the support of the ex-communist Bulgarian Socialist Party, said he would not resign.
The communist secret service, closely allied to the ex-Soviet KGB, had a network of 100,000 agents and informers. Its files have never been opened as they were in what used to be East Germany.
